title: Emergency Preparedness and Incident Management
description: This module introduces general workplace emergency preparedness, first response boundaries, evacuation, reporting, investigation and learning. Site-specific plans, local emergency numbers, legal reporting rules and responder competence always take precedence.

lessons.title: Emergency Planning and Responsibilities
lessons.summary: This module introduces general workplace emergency preparedness, first response boundaries, evacuation, reporting, investigation and learning. Site-specific plans, local emergency numbers, legal reporting rules and responder competence always take precedence.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: A site-specific emergency plan organizes actions for credible events such as fire, serious injury, explosion, chemical release, severe weather, structural failure or security incident.

The plan should define reporting methods, alarm signals, command, evacuation or shelter decisions, routes, assembly points, accountability, first aid, rescue interfaces, shutdown duties and emergency contacts.
Roles must be assigned to trained people, communicated to employees, contractors and visitors, coordinated with others sharing the workplace, and reviewed after changes or lessons learned.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A new project starts using chemicals but the emergency plan covers only fire. Work planning must add spill/release scenarios, isolation, evacuation or shelter, responder limits, equipment and external support.

questions.prompt: Why must an emergency plan be site specific?
questions.explanation: The response must match actual hazards, layout and resources.

questions.prompt: Who should know the plan?
questions.explanation: Everyone needs information relevant to their role.

questions.prompt: When should the plan be reviewed?
questions.explanation: Change can invalidate arrangements.

lessons.title: Emergency Alarms and Communication
lessons.summary: This module introduces general workplace emergency preparedness, first response boundaries, evacuation, reporting, investigation and learning. Site-specific plans, local emergency numbers, legal reporting rules and responder competence always take precedence.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Workers must know how to raise the alarm and recognize signals. Systems may include manual call points, sirens, public address, radios, internal numbers and external emergency calls.
Emergency messages should state the type and exact location, hazards present, casualties, access point, caller identity and assistance required. Use plain language and repeat-back where critical.
Alarm systems must be suitable for noise, visibility, language and disability needs, maintained and tested. Loss of normal power or communications requires backup arrangements.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A worker sees smoke but only messages a colleague. The correct action is to activate the site alarm and follow the emergency reporting procedure immediately.

questions.prompt: What should a person do on discovering an emergency?
options: Raise the alarm using the procedure
questions.explanation: Early warning protects others.

questions.prompt: Which location information is best?
questions.explanation: Responders need precise access information.

questions.prompt: What confirms a critical radio message?
questions.explanation: Repeat-back checks understanding.

lessons.title: Evacuation, Assembly and Accountability
lessons.summary: This module introduces general workplace emergency preparedness, first response boundaries, evacuation, reporting, investigation and learning. Site-specific plans, local emergency numbers, legal reporting rules and responder competence always take precedence.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: On an evacuation alarm, stop safely if immediate, use the designated route, walk without delay, do not use prohibited lifts and do not return for belongings.
Report to the assigned assembly point and remain for roll call. Supervisors should account for employees, contractors and visitors and report missing persons without attempting unauthorized rescue.

Routes and exits must be clear, marked, illuminated and suitable. Assistance arrangements are needed for persons with disabilities, language limitations or unfamiliarity. Re-entry requires official authorization.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A worker leaves the assembly point to collect a laptop. This undermines accountability and exposes the worker. They must remain until released by the authorized emergency controller.

questions.prompt: Where should evacuees report?
questions.explanation: Assembly enables accountability.

questions.prompt: Who may authorize re-entry?
options: The first person at the gate
questions.explanation: The hazard must be declared controlled.

questions.prompt: What if someone is missing?
questions.explanation: Unauthorized rescue may create more casualties.

lessons.title: Fire Emergency Response
lessons.summary: This module introduces general workplace emergency preparedness, first response boundaries, evacuation, reporting, investigation and learning. Site-specific plans, local emergency numbers, legal reporting rules and responder competence always take precedence.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Raise the alarm, call required assistance and evacuate. Close doors or isolate equipment only when this can be done immediately, safely and under the plan.
Portable extinguishers are for trained, authorized persons under defined conditions: a small manageable fire, correct extinguisher, safe escape route and no dangerous smoke or escalation.
Never fight a spreading fire, enter smoke, allow the fire between you and the exit, or delay evacuation. Fire watches and post-hot-work checks are prevention controls, not emergency substitutes.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A waste-bin fire produces increasing smoke. The worker activates the alarm and evacuates rather than attempting firefighting without training or a safe escape route.

questions.prompt: What comes first on discovering fire?
questions.explanation: Early alarm starts the response.

questions.prompt: When may an extinguisher be used?
questions.explanation: Firefighting must not compromise escape.

questions.prompt: What should happen with a spreading fire?
questions.explanation: Escalating fire requires professional response.

lessons.title: Medical Emergencies and First Aid
lessons.summary: This module introduces general workplace emergency preparedness, first response boundaries, evacuation, reporting, investigation and learning. Site-specific plans, local emergency numbers, legal reporting rules and responder competence always take precedence.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Protect yourself, make the area safe, call for trained first aid and emergency medical support, and send someone to guide responders.
Provide first aid only within training. Do not move a casualty unless leaving them creates greater danger, and do not give food, drink or medication unless directed by qualified personnel.
First-aid arrangements should reflect workplace hazards, workforce, shifts, remoteness and response time. Record required details while protecting medical privacy.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A worker collapses near energized equipment. Do not rush into danger. Isolate through the emergency procedure, call for help and provide first aid only when the area is safe.

questions.prompt: What is the rescuer's first priority?
questions.explanation: Rescuers must control danger first.

questions.prompt: Who should provide first aid?
questions.explanation: Treatment must stay within training.

questions.prompt: When may a casualty be moved?
options: When necessary due to greater danger or trained direction
questions.explanation: Unnecessary movement may worsen injury.

lessons.title: Chemical Spill and Release Response
lessons.summary: This module introduces general workplace emergency preparedness, first response boundaries, evacuation, reporting, investigation and learning. Site-specific plans, local emergency numbers, legal reporting rules and responder competence always take precedence.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Recognize the alarm and keep away from unknown vapour, liquid, dust or gas. Do not touch, smell or enter an affected area without training, authorization and suitable equipment.

Raise the alarm, identify the substance from a safe position if possible, isolate the area and eliminate ignition only when authorized and safe. Follow SDS and emergency-plan instructions for evacuation, shelter, spill control and decontamination.

Incidental small spills may be managed only by trained authorized workers within defined capability. An uncontrolled release, unknown atmosphere or IDLH potential requires specialist emergency response.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: An unknown gas alarm activates in a plant room. Workers evacuate and prevent entry. They do not attempt rescue or investigation without the required respiratory protection, monitoring and response competence.

questions.prompt: What should happen with an unknown release?
questions.explanation: Unknown exposure may be immediately dangerous.

questions.prompt: Where is chemical response information found?
questions.explanation: These documents define hazards and response.

questions.prompt: Who handles a major uncontrolled release?
questions.explanation: Emergency releases require specific competence and equipment.

lessons.title: Rescue Planning and Responder Safety
lessons.summary: This module introduces general workplace emergency preparedness, first response boundaries, evacuation, reporting, investigation and learning. Site-specific plans, local emergency numbers, legal reporting rules and responder competence always take precedence.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Rescue must be planned before high-risk work such as confined space, work at height, remote work or hazardous atmospheres. Calling public emergency services alone may not provide a timely task-specific rescue.
Define credible scenarios, alarm, access, competent rescuers, equipment, anchorage, retrieval, casualty care, communications, command and external-service interface.
Rescuers must not enter uncontrolled danger. Use non-entry rescue where designed and practicable. Test rescue arrangements through realistic practice and inspect equipment.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A suspended worker is hanging in a fall-arrest harness. The team uses the rehearsed rescue system; an untrained coworker does not climb out to improvise a rescue.

questions.prompt: When is rescue planned?
questions.explanation: Rescue readiness is a precondition for work.

questions.prompt: What is preferred where designed and practicable?
questions.explanation: It reduces responder exposure.

questions.prompt: May untrained workers improvise rescue?
questions.explanation: Improvised rescue can create additional casualties.

lessons.title: Incident and Near-Miss Reporting
lessons.summary: This module introduces general workplace emergency preparedness, first response boundaries, evacuation, reporting, investigation and learning. Site-specific plans, local emergency numbers, legal reporting rules and responder competence always take precedence.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: An incident may cause or have potential to cause injury, illness, damage or loss. A near miss causes no harm but had credible potential. Both provide learning opportunities.
First address emergency and immediate danger. Then notify through the company process and any applicable external requirements. Report promptly without hiding, altering or delaying facts.
Record what, where, when, who, conditions, actual/potential consequences and immediate actions. Use neutral factual language and protect personal information.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A tool falls from a platform but misses workers. Work stops, the drop zone is secured, the near miss is reported, and tool-tethering and edge controls are reviewed.

questions.prompt: What is a near miss?
options: No harm but potential for harm
questions.explanation: Potential severity makes it valuable for prevention.

questions.prompt: What should a report contain?
questions.explanation: Accurate facts support investigation.

questions.prompt: Should near misses be reported?
questions.explanation: They reveal control weaknesses before injury.

lessons.title: Scene Preservation and Basic Investigation
lessons.summary: This module introduces general workplace emergency preparedness, first response boundaries, evacuation, reporting, investigation and learning. Site-specific plans, local emergency numbers, legal reporting rules and responder competence always take precedence.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: After life safety and stabilization, preserve the scene when safe and required. Prevent unauthorized access and protect evidence from loss, movement, weather or cleanup.

Investigation aims to prevent recurrence, not simply assign blame. Collect photos where allowed, measurements, documents, equipment condition, witness accounts, sequence and environmental information.
Identify immediate, underlying and organizational causes. Corrective actions should address root contributors, use stronger controls, have owners and dates, and be verified for effectiveness.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: After a dropped-object incident, a supervisor removes the defective attachment before photos or examination. Unless needed for safety, evidence should remain controlled for investigation.

questions.prompt: What has priority over scene preservation?
questions.explanation: Emergency care and control come first.

questions.prompt: What is the investigation purpose?
questions.explanation: Learning and prevention are the goal.

questions.prompt: What should corrective actions include?
questions.explanation: Actions must be completed and verified.

lessons.title: Emergency Drills, Review and Improvement
lessons.summary: This module introduces general workplace emergency preparedness, first response boundaries, evacuation, reporting, investigation and learning. Site-specific plans, local emergency numbers, legal reporting rules and responder competence always take precedence.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Drills test whether people understand alarms, routes, roles, accountability, communication, equipment and coordination. They should be realistic, risk-controlled and appropriate to site hazards.
Brief observers, define objectives and do not create uncontrolled danger. Consider unannounced elements only under competent planning and site authorization.
Debrief participants, record timings and findings, assign improvement actions and update plans/training. Repeat drills after major changes or where performance shows weakness.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A drill shows contractors went to the wrong assembly point and the visitor list was unavailable. Actions update induction, signage, contractor briefings and accountability backup, then a follow-up drill verifies improvement.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a drill?
questions.explanation: Drills reveal practical gaps.

questions.prompt: What follows a drill?
questions.explanation: Learning must become improvement.

questions.prompt: When should another drill be considered?
options: After major change or weak performance
questions.explanation: Retesting verifies readiness.

title: Construction Safety Fundamentals
description: This module introduces common construction controls. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, client, equipment and task. Always apply the approved site system, competent design, manufacturer instructions and applicable law.

lessons.title: Site Induction, Access and Daily Coordination
lessons.summary: This module introduces common construction controls. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, client, equipment and task. Always apply the approved site system, competent design, manufacturer instructions and applicable law.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Before access, workers need site induction covering key hazards, prohibited activities, emergency arrangements, welfare, reporting, traffic routes and minimum PPE.
Verify identity, competence, medical/fitness requirements where applicable, training and authorization for assigned work. Visitors require control and escort according to the site system.
Daily pre-task coordination must address changing work fronts, simultaneous operations, deliveries, weather, access, permits and interfaces with other contractors.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A trained installer arrives at a new site and wants to start immediately. Previous experience does not replace site induction, access authorization and task briefing.

questions.prompt: What is required before starting at a new site?
questions.explanation: Workers must understand site-specific hazards and rules.

questions.prompt: What should daily coordination address?
questions.explanation: Construction hazards change continuously.

questions.prompt: How should visitors be managed?
options: Under the site access and escort system
questions.explanation: Visitors may not understand site hazards.

lessons.title: Permit to Work and Pre-task Briefing
lessons.summary: This module introduces common construction controls. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, client, equipment and task. Always apply the approved site system, competent design, manufacturer instructions and applicable law.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: A permit to work authorizes specified high-risk work at a defined location, time and conditions. It supports but never replaces physical controls.
Confirm scope, location, validity, isolations, competence, equipment, tests, emergency arrangements and signatures before starting. Suspend work when conditions or scope change.
The pre-task briefing explains steps, hazards, controls, roles, communication and stop-work conditions. Workers must be able to ask questions and confirm understanding.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A hot-work team moves to another building while keeping the old permit. Stop work and obtain review because location, combustibles, alarms and emergency arrangements may differ.

questions.prompt: Does a permit make work safe by itself?
questions.explanation: Controls must be implemented and verified.

questions.prompt: What if scope changes?
questions.explanation: Changed scope may invalidate the permit.

questions.prompt: What must a briefing allow?
questions.explanation: Understanding must be verified.

lessons.title: Excavation and Trenching Safety
lessons.summary: This module introduces common construction controls. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, client, equipment and task. Always apply the approved site system, competent design, manufacturer instructions and applicable law.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Before digging, identify underground services, obtain authorization, survey the area and plan access, spoil placement, plant movement, water control and emergency response.
A competent person must assess soil and excavation conditions and select protective systems such as sloping, benching, shoring or shielding according to the applicable design and rules.

Provide safe access/egress, edge protection, barriers, inspections and separation from vehicles and suspended loads. Stop for cracks, water, movement, damaged support, atmosphere concerns or changed conditions.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: Workers enter a trench after heavy rain without reinspection. Stop entry; water and soil conditions can change stability and require competent reassessment.

questions.prompt: What comes before digging?
questions.explanation: Buried services and ground risks must be assessed.

questions.prompt: Who selects the protective system?
questions.explanation: Excavation stability requires competence.

questions.prompt: What follows heavy rain?
questions.explanation: Rain can change ground stability.

lessons.title: Scaffolding Safety
lessons.summary: This module introduces common construction controls. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, client, equipment and task. Always apply the approved site system, competent design, manufacturer instructions and applicable law.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Scaffolds must be designed where required, erected, altered and dismantled by competent trained persons under suitable supervision and on adequate foundations.

Provide complete platforms, safe access, guardrails, midrails, toe boards, ties/bracing, suitable loading and protection from falling objects. Never climb cross-bracing or remove components without authorization.

Inspect before first use, after alteration, damaging events or adverse conditions, and at required intervals. Use the site tagging/status system but verify actual condition rather than relying on a tag alone.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A scaffold displays a green tag but a guardrail has been removed for material loading. Stop access and have the scaffold restored and reinspected.

questions.prompt: Who alters a scaffold?
questions.explanation: Unauthorized alteration can cause collapse or falls.

questions.prompt: Can a tag replace visual checks?
questions.explanation: Actual condition may have changed.

questions.prompt: May workers climb cross-bracing?
questions.explanation: Use designed safe access.

lessons.title: Ladders and Stepladders
lessons.summary: This module introduces common construction controls. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, client, equipment and task. Always apply the approved site system, competent design, manufacturer instructions and applicable law.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Use ladders only when the risk assessment shows they are suitable, commonly for low-risk short-duration work. A safer platform or access system may be required.
Select the correct type and length, inspect before use, place on firm level ground, secure against movement and protect from doors, vehicles and electrical hazards.

Maintain three points of contact while climbing and where practicable at the work position. Do not overreach, stand on prohibited steps, carry awkward loads or use a closed stepladder as a leaning ladder.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A worker stands on the top step and leans sideways while drilling. Stop and provide a suitable platform or repositioned access system.

questions.prompt: When may a ladder be suitable?
questions.explanation: Ladders are not automatically the first choice.

questions.prompt: What contact is expected while climbing?
questions.explanation: Stable contact reduces fall risk.

questions.prompt: What should a worker do instead of overreaching?
options: Ask someone to hold a tool
questions.explanation: The ladder must be positioned for safe reach.

lessons.title: Confined Space Entry
lessons.summary: This module introduces common construction controls. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, client, equipment and task. Always apply the approved site system, competent design, manufacturer instructions and applicable law.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Avoid confined-space entry where practicable. Identify spaces and foreseeable risks such as oxygen deficiency, toxic/flammable atmosphere, engulfment, flooding, heat, mechanical energy and restricted rescue.

Where entry is required, use the approved permit program: isolate hazards, test the atmosphere, ventilate, control ignition, provide communication, competent entrants/attendant/supervisor and continuous or periodic monitoring as assessed.
A task-specific rescue plan and capable rescue service must be ready before entry. Never attempt spontaneous entry rescue without required training and equipment.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A worker collapses inside a tank and a coworker moves to enter without breathing equipment. The attendant raises the alarm and initiates the planned rescue instead.

questions.prompt: Preferred confined-space control?
questions.explanation: Avoidance eliminates entry exposure.

questions.prompt: What is needed before entry?
options: Permit controls, testing and rescue readiness
questions.explanation: Multiple hazards require a complete system.

questions.prompt: May an untrained coworker enter for rescue?
questions.explanation: Unplanned rescue often creates additional casualties.

lessons.title: Hot Work, Welding and Cutting
lessons.summary: This module introduces common construction controls. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, client, equipment and task. Always apply the approved site system, competent design, manufacturer instructions and applicable law.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Hot work may create fire, explosion, fumes, radiation, burns and compressed-gas hazards. Use the applicable permit and approved work area.
Remove or protect combustibles, control openings and spark travel, provide ventilation, screens, suitable extinguishers, trained fire watch where required and post-work monitoring.

Inspect cylinders, regulators, hoses, leads and return paths. Secure cylinders upright, separate incompatible gases as required, protect valves and follow correct lighting, shutdown and leak-response procedures.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: Cutting sparks pass through a floor opening to combustible waste below. Stop work, control the lower level and spark path, then revalidate the permit.

questions.prompt: What must be controlled beyond the immediate area?
questions.explanation: Hot particles may ignite hidden combustibles.

questions.prompt: What protects nearby persons from arc radiation?
questions.explanation: Arc radiation can injure eyes and skin.

questions.prompt: What if controls change?
questions.explanation: Permit conditions must remain valid.

lessons.title: Lifting and Rigging on Construction Sites
lessons.summary: This module introduces common construction controls. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, client, equipment and task. Always apply the approved site system, competent design, manufacturer instructions and applicable law.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: A competent lift plan must address the load, centre of gravity, lifting points, crane/equipment capacity and configuration, ground, setup, route, weather and nearby structures or power lines.
Use competent operators, riggers and signalers; certified/inspected equipment; correct slings and accessories; protected edges; tag lines where appropriate; and a secured exclusion zone.
Conduct a pre-lift briefing and trial/tension check where appropriate. Stop for overload indication, unstable load, loss of communication, equipment/person intrusion or changing conditions.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A load rotates and a worker tries to control it by hand under the hook. Stop and revise rigging/tag-line arrangements while keeping people out of the fall zone.

questions.prompt: What determines rigging selection?
questions.explanation: Rigging must match load, configuration and capacity.

questions.prompt: Who gives routine signals?
questions.explanation: Conflicting signals are dangerous.

questions.prompt: When must the lift stop?
questions.explanation: Control cannot continue without reliable signals.

lessons.title: Temporary Electrical Installations
lessons.summary: This module introduces common construction controls. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, client, equipment and task. Always apply the approved site system, competent design, manufacturer instructions and applicable law.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Temporary electrical systems still require proper design, distribution, overcurrent and earth/ground protection, suitable enclosures and installation by authorized qualified persons.
Protect cables from water, sharp edges, crushing, traffic, heat and trip hazards. Use suitable connectors and approved protection devices; never insert bare wires or make makeshift joints.
Inspect equipment and distribution boards, keep covers closed and access controlled, identify circuits, remove defects from service and remove temporary wiring when no longer required.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: An extension lead has taped damage and lies across a wet route. Isolate and remove it, control the area and arrange authorized replacement and safe routing.

questions.prompt: Who installs or repairs temporary power?
questions.explanation: Temporary does not mean unregulated.

questions.prompt: Can a taped damaged cable remain in use?
questions.explanation: Defective insulation requires removal and proper repair/replacement.

questions.prompt: Where should cables be routed?
questions.explanation: Routing prevents electrical and physical damage.

lessons.title: Heat Stress and Extreme Weather
lessons.summary: This module introduces common construction controls. Requirements vary by jurisdiction, client, equipment and task. Always apply the approved site system, competent design, manufacturer instructions and applicable law.

sections.heading: Core Learning
points: Assess temperature, humidity, radiant heat, air movement, workload, clothing/PPE, acclimatization, health, hydration and duration. Use a suitable heat-stress method and local requirements.
Provide shade/cooling, water, work-rest schedules, acclimatization, task timing, buddy monitoring, training and emergency response. New or returning workers may need gradual exposure.
Monitor wind, lightning, rain, dust and poor visibility for cranes, MEWPs, roofs, scaffolds and lifting. Stop when manufacturer, site or regulatory limits are exceeded or conditions become unsafe.

sections.heading: Practical Scenario
points: A new worker performs heavy roof work during peak heat and becomes confused. Stop work, move the person to a safe cool area, raise medical help and follow the heat-emergency procedure.

questions.prompt: Which worker may be at higher heat risk?
questions.explanation: Acclimatization reduces but does not remove risk.

questions.prompt: What is a serious warning sign?
questions.explanation: Heat illness can become life-threatening.

questions.prompt: What if wind exceeds equipment/site limits?
questions.explanation: Weather limits protect stability and control.

finalAssessment.explanation: Correct answer: Locate services and authorize

finalAssessment.explanation: Correct answer: Assessed low-risk short duration
Correct answer: Testing isolation rescue readiness

finalAssessment.explanation: Correct answer: Stop and control both levels
Correct answer: Anyone following site stop-work process
